title: Function of the digestive system
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
caveat: Digestive physiology review. Detailed nutrition claim checks delegated to the nutrition reviewer.

title: Nutrition and Digestive Physiology of the Broiler Chick: State of the Art and Outlook
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Early digestive immaturity; changing enzyme secretion and absorptive capacity; early feeding/water importance; early growth effects not necessarily maintained at market age.
caveat: Review of early chick digestion, not an olive leaf intervention. Early developmental effects need not persist to market age.
crossReviewEvidence: Full primary review text from PMC returned in web search; abstract, introduction, maturation and nutrient utilization/conclusion sections consulted. Direct publisher HTML returned 429, subsequent PMC direct open gave bot-check.

title: The chicken gastrointestinal microbiome
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Chicken gastrointestinal microbiome, spatial/temporal variability and relationships with nutrition and immunity.
caveat: Contextual review; does not demonstrate an olive leaf effect.

title: Alternatives to antibiotics for maximizing growth performance and feed efficiency in poultry: a review
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Historically proposed AGP mechanisms, uncertainty over a unique mechanism, alternative classes and context-dependent efficacy.
caveat: Contextual review; not evidence that every phytogenic product is an established antibiotic replacement. Individual trial tables were not comprehensively audited.
crossReviewEvidence: Publisher full PDF accessible (20 pages); abstract and mechanism/alternative categories sections consulted, not all individual trial tables.

title: The Status of Genetic Resources and Olive Breeding in Tunisia
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: More than 200 olive varieties in Tunisian collections; Chemlali and Chetoui are among the major cultivars.
caveat: Economic rankings and production statistics reflect the sources available in 2022. The manuscript appropriately avoids presenting them as current statistics.

title: Ross Broiler Nutrition Specifications 2022
metadataSource: Official PDF cover, footers and copyright checked by nutrition reviewer
checkedClaims: Guidelines require adjustment to local conditions, final product, ingredients, sex, age/weight and carcass objectives. Standardized ileal digestible amino acids, phase-specific AME, minerals and vitamin recommendations.
caveat: Industry guidance, not an olive-leaf intervention experiment. Recommendations require adaptation to the actual flock and production objectives.
crossReviewEvidence: Official full PDF downloaded successfully; introduction and phase-specific tables consulted. Cover, footers and copyright verify 2022.

title: Ross Broiler Management Handbook
metadataSource: Official PDF cover, footers and copyright checked by nutrition reviewer
checkedClaims: Starter at least 10 days (p52); finisher feeds represent most total feed intake and feeding cost (p52); feeding strategy depends on product, economics, sex, weight and age (p51); pellet/fines/particle-size effects (p54); fungal/toxin grain quality and digestible nutrient balance (p56); unrestricted quality water and measurement, spillage, heat, drinking systems (p57,60).
caveat: Industry guidance, not an olive-leaf intervention experiment. Recommendations require adaptation to the actual flock and production objectives.
crossReviewEvidence: Official full PDF downloaded successfully by normal HTTP after web tool returned 403. Targeted sections consulted: pages 24, 51–52, 54, 56–57 and 60. Cover and copyright verify 2025, edition code 0325-V1.

title: Pharmacognosy and Antioxidant Activity of Pruned Leaves from the Unexplored <i>Olea europaea</i> L. 'Lavagnina' (Liguria, Italy).
metadataSource: Europe PMC/PubMed primary article record
checkedClaims: Lavagnina cultivar: leaf morphology and phenolic compounds in palisade parenchyma and trichome stalk cells.
Methanolic and 70 percent ethanol extracts show antioxidant activity; HAE significantly outperformed other extracts only in the DPPH assay.
caveat: Name the DPPH assay when stating superiority. Chemical in vitro activity is not evidence of in vivo protection; this is not a poultry trial.

title: Polyphenol deposition in leaf hairs of Olea Europaea (OLeaceae) andQUercus Ilex (Fagaceae)
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Subcellular localization of polyphenols in Olea and Quercus leaf hairs; fluorescence shifts from cytoplasm to cell walls during maturation.
caveat: Plant anatomy research, not an extraction or poultry experiment. No lawful open PDF identified.

title: Trichome layers versus dehaired lamina of Olea europaea leaves: differences in flavonoid distribution, UV-absorbing capacity, and wax yield
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Six cultivars: greater flavonoid diversity in dehaired lamina; higher total flavonoids per unit mass in trichomes; quercetin and quercetin-3-O-rhamnoside associated with trichomes.
caveat: Publisher abstract checked; full text not obtained. Does not directly demonstrate improved extraction yield.

title: Antimicrobial activity of commercial Olea europaea (olive) leaf extract
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: 122 microorganisms tested; activity primarily against C. jejuni, H. pylori, S. aureus and MRSA; no uniform broad-spectrum activity.
caveat: Commercial extract tested in vitro; no demonstrated efficacy in chickens.

title: Immunomodulatory properties of Olea europaea leaf extract in intestinal inflammation
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Two mouse colitis models, cell cultures and human explants; reduced inflammatory mediators and restored expression of ZO-1, MUC-2 and TFF-3.
caveat: Original bibliography omitted five coauthors: Talhaoui, Gomez-Caravaca, Segura-Carretero, Rodriguez-Cabezas and Monteleone. Correct the entry. Not an avian study. Publisher abstract read, not the full text.

title: Olive (Olea europaea L.) Leaf Polyphenols Improve Insulin Sensitivity in Middle-Aged Overweight Men: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Randomized crossover trial in 46 overweight men; improved insulin sensitivity and beta-cell responsiveness, without changes in several other outcomes.
caveat: Human population and standardized supplement. Does not demonstrate general hypoglycemia or an avian effect. Full-text XML retrieved; numbers checked against the abstract.

title: Olive leaf extract effect on cardiometabolic profile among adults with prehypertension and hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Five trials, 325 adults; some favorable blood-pressure findings but conclusions limited by sample sizes and heterogeneity.
caveat: Different comparators, preparations and doses. Do not generalize to all extracts or to poultry. Full-text XML retrieved; synthesis checked against the abstract.

title: The effects of olive leaf extract on cardiovascular risk factors in the general adult population: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Twelve studies, 819 participants; pooled reductions in triglycerides and systolic blood pressure; no meaningful overall improvement in glycemic or inflammatory variables.
caveat: Human results and subgroup findings. Low to very low certainty for several outcomes. Full-text XML retrieved; synthesis checked against the abstract.

title: Use of Oleuropein and Hydroxytyrosol for Cancer Prevention and Treatment: Considerations about How Bioavailability and Metabolism Impact Their Adoption in Clinical Routine
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Review of antiproliferative effects of oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol; limited bioavailability and the gap between experimental models and clinical use are explicitly discussed.
caveat: Mechanistic and preclinical review. Not clinical proof of anticancer efficacy or direct evidence relevant to broiler growth.

title: Advances in bioactivity and health benefits of olive leaf: an updated review
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Updated review of olive-leaf bioactivities and preparations; need for more rigorous clinical trials and long-term toxicity data.
caveat: Its search covers 2015-2025 despite publication in 2026; it does not itself cover all 2026 research. Add volume 25 and pages 4989-5025.

title: Metabolic and inflammatory effects of oleuropein and olive leaf extract: a systematic review and meta-analysis
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Eleven adult RCTs: four short-term and seven continuous-intake trials; null pooled metabolic results in continuous parallel-design trials; scarce, low-certainty inflammatory evidence.
caveat: Correct author name parsing to Peres, Kathleen Kruger and da Mata, Isabella Rosa. Abstract only; do not imply all eleven trials were pooled.

title: Efficacy of Olive Leaf Extract in Improving Blood Pressure in Pre‐Hypertensive and Hypertensive Individuals: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Three studies, 248 prehypertensive/hypertensive participants; systolic signal and high-dose subgroup effect, with explicit methodological limitations.
caveat: The overall pre/post analysis reports nonsignificant diastolic change, p=0.07, despite the abstract wording. Do not interpret the overall finding as a uniform placebo-controlled effect. Institutional PDF identified; download to be confirmed.

title: Chemical and structural heterogeneity of olive leaves and their trichomes
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Chemical and structural heterogeneity of trichomes and leaf sides; possible functional effects on water/solute interactions are discussed.
caveat: An effect on extraction yield is an inference, not a measurement in this article. Use conditional wording.

title: Microscopic attributes of Olea europaea L. leaves and bioclimatology: the case of Galicia, western Iberian Peninsula
metadataSource: Crossref DOI record; publisher/Europe PMC cross-check where available
checkedClaims: Five Galician varieties; intervarietal differences in cuticle, leaf blade and trichomes; abaxial stomata and differentiated mesophyll.
caveat: Correct title ending to: the case of Galicia, western Iberian Peninsula. Anatomical associations do not experimentally demonstrate drought tolerance.
